issues.description: The problem statement and UML expect Stock to provide a method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), but the template Stock.java defines addItem(StockIngredient) instead. This name/signature mismatch will prevent students from following the specification or using the expected method name (e.g., in acceptSupplyDelivery) and will cause compilation errors or confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the method in the template from addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), or add a forwarding method addToStockIngredients that calls addItem. Ensure the template matches the method name and signature used in the problem statement/UML and the solution.

issues.description: The problem statement's UML and the reference solution expect a Stock method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), but the template repository's Stock class provides a method named addItem(StockIngredient). This mismatched identifier for the same conceptual operation (adding a StockIngredient to the stock) can confuse students: the problem text and solution refer to addToStockIngredients while the starter code uses addItem, increasing extraneous cognitive load and making it harder to map requirements to the provided API.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent method name across all artifacts. Rename the template's Stock.addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) (or alternatively update problem and solution to use addItem) so the starter code API matches the problem description and the reference solution.
